notes: The circuit image shows no breadboard, but the manual lists 2 mini breadboards. I assumed bb1 is the shared I2C bus: SDA (A4) from both boards meets in column 5 and SCL (A5) in column 10. bb2 carries the two 4.7k pull-ups and a 3V3 rail fed from the reader's 3V pin. Two bridging jumpers (wire7 for SDA, wire8 for SCL) connect the two breadboards. This split is my own layout choice.
The manual lists 10 jumper wires. The pictured circuit with this layout needs 8: 3 on the reader, 2 on the writer, 1 for GND, and 2 bridging the breadboards.
The catalogue breadboard is full-size, so mini-breadboard hole names are approximate.
The image labels the reader supply pin '3V', which I mapped to the Nano Every '3V3' port. GND is mapped to 'GND1' on both boards.
In the image, the teal A5 line (SCL) and the yellow A4 line (SDA) cross without connecting. Each pull-up resistor goes to its own line only.
The manual says SDA is A4 and SCL is A5. Both boards are powered and programmed over USB from a computer, so each has a USB cable. The reader needs only power.
